How the proxy works:
- **Allowed paths:** built once at startup from `listChallengeSummaries()` and `challengePath()`, so there's no second list of challenges.
- **Matching:** the requested path must equal an allowed path exactly. It's compared as received, without decoding or changing case.
- **Valid paths:** pass through untouched.
- **Everything else:** gets a direct `404` with the text "Challenge not found." and `Cache-Control: no-store`. It is never redirected or rewritten.
- **Scope:** the matcher is `"/challenges/:challengeId"` only.
- **Imports:** only `next/server`, the public catalog and the path helper.

The route itself, `generateStaticParams()` and the page's own `notFound()` check are unchanged.

## Tests

- **Proxy request handling** (unit tests):
  - Challenge 001 and every catalog path pass through.
  - Query strings on valid paths pass through, including `?_rsc=`.
  - These get a 404 and are never redirected or rewritten:
    - wrong case (`CHALLENGE-001`, `Challenge-001`, `chALLenge-001`);
    - unknown IDs (`challenge-999`, `__proto__`, `constructor`);
    - other encodings (`challenge%2D001`, `challenge%2d001`, `%63hallenge-001`, `challenge-001%20`, `challenge-001%00`);
    - invalid IDs with query strings.
- **Matcher scope:** the proxy does not run on `/`, `/challenges`, the diagnosis API (in either case), `/_next/static`, `/_next/image`, `/monaco/…`, `/favicon.ico` or similar-looking paths.
- **The tests catch regressions.** I temporarily made four deliberate changes, one at a time, and each made tests fail:
  - ignoring case;
  - decoding the path;
  - widening the matcher;
  - redirecting instead of returning 404.

  The file was restored byte for byte afterwards.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| All challenge tests | 60/60 |
| Full suite | 531/531, 0 failed, 0 skipped |
| Typecheck / lint | both pass |
| Production build | passes; output now lists "ƒ Proxy (Middleware)", and `/challenges/challenge-001` is still prebuilt static |
| Homepage | byte-identical (73,044 bytes) |
| Diagnosis, engine, session, backend, data, types, `next.config.ts` | unchanged |

## Live HTTP behaviour

| Sequence | Result |
|---|---|
| A: fresh build, wrong case, then valid | 404, then 200, 200 |
| B: fresh build, valid, two wrong-case variants, valid | 200, 404, 404, 200 |
| C: fresh build, 7 unknown or alternately encoded IDs, then valid | 404 ×7, then 200 |
| D: restart without rebuilding, A–C repeated plus extra paths | Rejected IDs 404 and valid ones 200, as in A–C. Extra paths: `/`, `/challenges`, `/challenges/` and `?x=1` → 200; `/CHALLENGES/challenge-001` and `/challenges/challenge-001/extra` → Next's normal 404 page. |

- **Client navigation requests** (the RSC requests the router sends): the valid ID returns 200 `text/x-component`; wrong-case and unknown IDs return a plain 404.
- **Browser flow:**
  - From `/challenges`, Tab then Enter opens `/challenges/challenge-001` with the editor, overview, 5 root-cause options and the submit button.
  - No third-party requests and no console errors.
- **Diagnosis:** a request from the challenge page got the same "invalid answer" 400 as before; the proxy never matches the API.

## Cache behaviour

After all the sequences, the route cache held only the fixed set of entries:
- `/`, `/challenges` and `/challenges/challenge-001`;
- one shared not-found page, from the unrelated paths that didn't match any route.

There was no wrong-case entry, no entry per unknown ID, and the real challenge's entry stayed at status 200.

## Remaining risks

- **Bad links get a bare page.** An invalid challenge URL shows a plain-text 404 instead of the styled not-found page. Clicking a link to one in the app makes the browser load that plain 404 page in full. This was your stated preference; a rewrite to the styled page would need its own status check.
- **The allowed list is fixed at startup.** It's built from the catalog when the server starts, so a registry that adds challenges at runtime will need the proxy updated.
- **The proxy runs before every challenge request.** It's one exact lookup in a set. It does bundle Challenge 001's public scenario into the server-side proxy code; that data never reaches the browser.
- **Wrong-case paths that don't match the proxy.** `/CHALLENGES/challenge-001` isn't matched, but it falls to Next's shared static 404 page, so it adds no per-path cache entries.
- **Still needs separate handling:** the `/` vs `/challenges/challenge-001` duplicate URL, the future learner-status work against `ensureStatic = "navigation"`, and `AppHeader` on `/challenges`.

Everything else is either work for when sessions are wired in, or hardening needed before a second challenge. Challenge 001 itself is unaffected by every frontend issue below.

## 1. Commits and ancestry

- **Integration worktree:** branch `integration/v1-challenge-001` at `16c01700…`, clean.

- **Ancestry:** a straight line on top of `02e1c2b` (PR #2), which integration already merged, so that is the merge base. None of the four commits is in integration yet.
- **Overlap with our work:** none of his commits touches `src/server/diagnosis`, `src/app`, `src/components`, `src/lib`, `src/types` or `src/data`.

**Combined-code test:** I built the simulated merge in a throwaway worktree and ran the checks there. Nothing was merged, and the throwaway worktree has been removed.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Tests | 1,838 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped |
| Lint | passes |
| Typecheck | **fails, 2 errors**, both in `tests/challenges/compatibility.test.ts` at lines 73 and 106: "Property 'appOrigin' is missing … required in type 'DiagnosisHandlerOptions'" |
| Production build | couldn't run; Turbopack wouldn't resolve `next` through the linked `node_modules` folder in my test setup |

- **Why the type error:** our origin fix `89c61d7` made `appOrigin` a required option, and his branch predates that.
- **Why the tests still pass:** at runtime the missing option is `undefined`, and the handler falls back to its development behaviour.
- **The skipped test:** a scan of the built client output for answer-key text, which needs a production build. Per Habin's doc it only becomes meaningful once a route imports the registry.

## 2. Compatibility issues

| # | Area | Issue | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | Diagnosis | Combined typecheck fails (above). Fix: add `appOrigin: null` to both handler options in `compatibility.test.ts`. | **Blocker** for a clean merge (2 lines) |
| E2 | Sessions / auth | Habin's handlers use a different Origin and cookie policy from the hardened diagnosis endpoint (details below). | **Important**; must be fixed before the routes are mounted |
| A1 | `serverLogId` | The loader allows requests with no `serverLogId`, but the shared type and two UI sites assume one exists (details below). | **Important** before a second challenge; no effect on Challenge 001, where all 16 requests have one |
| B1 | Selectors | Some `querySelector` calls build selectors from data the loader accepts, so certain characters crash them (details below). | **Important** before new challenges; Challenge 001's names and IDs are safe |
| B2 | Tab IDs | Different file names can produce the same editor tab ID. `getTabId` (`EditorTabs.tsx:6`) replaces every non-alphanumeric character with `-`, so `a-b.ts`, `a_b.ts` and `a.b.ts` share an ID, and so do most non-Latin names (`日本語.ts`, `ファイル.ts`). The result is duplicate DOM IDs, so focus and scrolling can land on the wrong tab. | Minor to important |
| C1 | Monaco | Habin's percent-escape analysis was made against an older editor that put the path into the URI unencoded. Integration (`89a622f`, `src/lib/monaco-models.ts:46–53`) already encodes each segment. | Minor (decision and doc update) |
| D1 | Sessions client | No frontend uses learner sessions yet, and several pieces are missing (details below). | **Important**; this is the integration work itself |
| E3 | Diagnosis client | `src/lib/diagnosis/client.ts:41` returns any body shaped like `{status, message}` and ignores the HTTP status. So the proposed 401, 404 and 409 responses would show as a generic error the UI can't act on. The extra `code` field in the error body is harmless, since the shape check at `response.ts:77` only requires `message`. | **Important** when diagnosis moves onto the service |
| E4 | `Idempotency-Key` | The client sends only `Content-Type`. It needs a UUID generated per submit and reused for a retry of the same click. Compatible with our origin and content-type checks. | Important, at the same step |
| F1 | Loader vs catalog | The data now has two sources of truth: `page.tsx` and the diagnosis route import Challenge 001 directly, and the Challenge Library's `src/lib/challenge-catalog.ts` (not in integration) does too. The registry's `list()` and `getPublic()` mirror the catalog, but `getPublic` returns `undefined` where the catalog returns `null`. | Minor |
| F2 | Loader schema | The loader adapts `challenge001` unchanged, and its tests compare against the current handler. Its public view returns a `WorkspaceScenario` unchanged, apart from omitting an absent `serverLogId` (A1). | None found |

**E2 in detail.** `handlers.ts:106–117` compares the request's `Origin` with `new URL(request.url).origin`, and `:49` sets `Secure` from `request.url`'s scheme. Our diagnosis endpoint instead uses `BUGLAB_APP_ORIGIN` through `src/server/diagnosis/origin.ts`. Our earlier review found that under `next start`, `request.url` takes its host and port from the server's bind address and its scheme from the client-supplied `X-Forwarded-Proto`. So once mounted:
- legitimate requests would get a 403 whenever the browser's host differs from the bind address: `127.0.0.1` against `localhost`, a LAN IP, or a TLS proxy;
- the `Secure` cookie decision would trust a header any client can set.

The two policies also differ when `Origin` is missing: the handlers refuse unless `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`, while diagnosis allows it.

**A1 in detail.** `src/types/investigation.ts:24` declares `serverLogId: string` as required, and two places assume it exists:
- `InvestigationConsole.tsx:60` builds a `Map` keyed by it, so several requests without one would collide under the key `undefined`;
- `RequestDetails.tsx:131–132` always renders "View in Logs (…)" and calls `onShowLog(undefined)`.

**B1 in detail.** The loader accepts `"` in paths; only `< > : " | ? *` are left to the author, per `paths.ts:56`. It only requires log, request and option IDs to be non-blank. So:
- `FileExplorer.tsx:68` uses `[data-path="${path}"]`. A path like `quo"te.md` makes the selector invalid, and `querySelector` throws during keyboard navigation.
- The same pattern applies to challenge-supplied IDs:
  - `[data-option-id="${id}"]` in `useListboxNavigation.ts:22,60` and `InvestigationConsole.tsx:82`;
  - `[data-remove-id="${id}"]` in `useRemovalFocus.ts:22`, where evidence IDs are `log:<logId>`.
- Backslashes and control characters are refused by the loader, so only quotes are reachable today.

**C1 in detail.** I round-tripped 23 paths through Monaco's own `URI` class with integration's encoding:
- every literal path survives exactly: `50%20off.md`, `%2e%2e/x.md`, `a%2fb.md`, `caf%C3%A9.md`, `%41.md`, `%252e.md`, `?`, `#`, quotes, backslashes, CJK and emoji;
- there are no collisions;
- only empty segments collapse (`a//b`, leading or trailing `/`), and the loader refuses those anyway.

With the old unencoded form, I reproduced exactly the decoding collisions Habin's doc describes. His extra checks on decoded paths are now unnecessary but harmless; they just refuse a few more names. His own comment at `paths.ts:44` anticipates removing them once the editor encodes. The doc's statement that "`50%20off.md` and `50 off.md` open the same buffer" is outdated for integration.

**D1 in detail.** What's missing:
- **Calls to the session endpoints:** `POST /api/learner`, then `POST` and `GET /api/challenges/:id/session`.
- **A way to restore a completed result after a refresh:**
  - the engine reducer has only a payload-less `DIAGNOSIS_ACCEPTED` (`src/engine/types.ts:79`);
  - `ChallengeSessionProvider` still has `investigationStarted` hard-coded to true.
- **Restoring the submitted evidence** into the investigation controller.
- **Handling `restartRequired` and `restarted`**, which mean clearing local evidence, notes and hypotheses.

Cookies are compatible: `buglab_learner` and the current `buglab_attempt` are both `HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/api`, and the proposed diagnosis change (his section 11.1) retires `buglab_attempt`.

## 3. Minimal frontend changes (ours)

1. **A1:** make `serverLogId?: string` optional, skip requests without one when building the map, and hide "View in Logs" when it's absent.
2. **B1:**
   - stop interpolating values into selectors; find elements by comparing `element.dataset.path`, `.optionId` or `.removeId` directly (one small helper), or keep a ref map;
   - avoid `CSS.escape`, which Node-based tests don't have.
3. **B2:** derive tab IDs from something unique, such as an index or a URL-safe encoding of the path, not a lossy replacement.
4. **E3 and E4, when diagnosis moves onto the service:**
   - pass the HTTP status, or the response's `code`, through the client, so a 409 for an outdated session can trigger "start again";
   - add `Idempotency-Key`.
5. **D1, after the routes are mounted:**
   - a small session client;
   - a "completion restored" engine action that carries the server's completion data;
   - workspace hydration;
   - restart handling.

## 4. Backend changes for Habin

1. **E1:** add `appOrigin: null` at `compatibility.test.ts` lines 73 and 106. Alternatively, rebase onto `integration/v1-challenge-001` and adjust there.
2. **E2:** make the handlers use `isSameOriginRequest` and `shouldSetSecureCookie` from `src/server/diagnosis/origin.ts`, driven by `BUGLAB_APP_ORIGIN`, before anything is mounted. Agree one policy for requests with no `Origin`.
3. **C1:** update section 8.3 and the "awaiting confirmation" note to reflect the encoded model URIs. Optionally drop the decoded-path checks if you choose purely literal paths.
4. **B1 (optional):** restrict log, request and option IDs to a safe pattern in the loader as defence in depth. Paths can't be restricted that way, so the frontend fix is still needed.
5. **Base his section 11.1 work** (diagnosis on the service) on integration. `src/server/diagnosis/handler.ts` and the diagnosis `route.ts` both changed in `89c61d7`, which adds the `appOrigin` parameter, so starting from an older base will conflict.

## 5. Potential Git conflicts

- **Merging his branch now:** none. The merge is textually clean, and only the E1 type error appears.
- **Future:**
  - his diagnosis integration against `handler.ts` and `route.ts`, unless he bases it on integration;
  - the Challenge Library branch, once the catalog is moved onto the registry: `challenge-catalog.ts` and its source-guard test forbid `@/server/` imports, and his guard test forbids imports from outside `src/server`. Both guards will need agreed exceptions.
  - The session-log files merge cleanly.

## 6. Safest order

1. Habin fixes E1, then merge his branch into integration with `--no-ff`. Run the full validation, including a real production build.
2. Habin fixes E2 and C1, docs only for C1.
3. We make the small frontend hardening changes (A1, B1, B2) on a branch from integration. None of them depends on the backend.
4. Decide the open points (below).
5. Habin mounts the registry and the session routes, after a durable-store decision, and does the section 11.1 diagnosis work on integration.
6. We add the session client, completion restore, `Idempotency-Key` and status-aware errors (D1, E3, E4).
7. Merge the Challenge Library and move the catalog onto `registry.list()` and `getPublic()`.

## 7. Questions to settle with Habin

- **Origin policy:** one shared policy for the handlers and diagnosis (E2), including whether non-browser clients without an `Origin` header are allowed.
- **Percent escapes:** keep the stricter decoded-path checks (safe and harmless) or go purely literal now that the editor encodes. I'd keep them for now; dropping them is a separate cleanup.
- **Padded and trailing-dot path segments:** keep refusing them?
- **Retrying a completed challenge:** may a learner retry one?
- **Durable store and deployment:** which store, and the real deployment topology, before mounting.
- **Who makes the A1 and B1 frontend changes, and when.** They're in our files.

I changed no files and made no merges, cherry-picks or commits. The only Git changes are the fetched remote-tracking ref `origin/feature/learner-session-foundation` and an unreferenced simulation commit (`c09d9fb`) that Git will clean up on its own. The case-file design is ready for your review, and all automated checks pass. But I found one real bug before you approve: after the workspace is left with the header's "Challenges" link and opened again from the library, the code editor doesn't load. The bug is in the existing editor code, but the uncommitted Milestone 5A header link is what makes it reachable. Details below. Nothing is committed; HEAD is still `eeb6ea0`.

## Files changed this round

- `src/components/challenge/ChallengeLibrary.tsx`: the editorial hero, a reading-width column, the "Open investigation" button and the grid rule.
- `src/components/challenge/ChallengeCard.tsx`: the case-file layout.

The rest of 5A (header, mobile nav fix, skip links, icons) is unchanged.

## The design

- **Hero:** no border box. A blue mono "CHALLENGE LIBRARY" label, the headline "Every bug has a story." (`text-4xl` on desktop), and a one-sentence subtitle. Content sits in a centred column about 1,024px wide.
- **Case-file card:**
  - a workspace-style title strip with a bug icon and "Challenge 001";
  - a larger title (`text-xl`) that turns blue on hover;
  - the real incident text in a quiet **Incident report** panel, with a small red dot rather than a red border;
  - a metadata column using the workspace's own labels: **Difficulty**, **Est. time**, **Topics**.
- **Button:** a solid BugLab-blue "Open investigation →" at the bottom of the metadata column, full width on phones. It's part of the single card link, so there are no nested controls.
- **One card or many:** a single challenge spans the column. From two challenges up, cards pair off on wide screens (`lg:grid-cols-2`). Each card arranges itself by its own width: side by side when wide, stacked when narrow.
- **Interaction:** 150ms colour changes only, and the arrow nudge is disabled for users who prefer reduced motion. The focus ring and border are as before.

## Results

|---|---|
| Challenge and header tests | 66/66 |
| Full suite | 537/537, 0 failed, 0 skipped |
| Typecheck / lint | both pass |
| Production build | passes |
| Routes, catalog, data, engine, server, workspace, proxy, dependencies | unchanged |

**Browser** (production build, headless Chrome):

| Width | Card layout | Page scrolls sideways? | Header nav clipped? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 320 | stacked | no | no |
| 375 | stacked | no | no |
| 820 | side by side | no | no |
| 1440 | side by side, 976px card | no | no |

- **Keyboard:** focus goes to the skip link, then "Challenges", then the card (named "Broken User Sessions"). Each shows a 2px outline, and the card's border turns blue when focused.
- **Mouse:**
  - hovering the button dims it to 85% blue; its dark text on blue is high contrast;
  - clicking it opens `/challenges/challenge-001`.
- **Library → Challenge 001 → Library:** works.
- **Workspace and diagnosis:** the editor loads, all 5 root-cause options are there, a diagnosis request gets the usual 400, and `/` is unaffected.

## The editor bug

**What goes wrong:**
- **Working paths:** reaching the workspace from a fresh page load works, and so does leaving it with the browser's back button.
- **Failing path:** library → workspace → "Challenges" in the header → card. On the second visit the editor panel stays empty, and Monaco throws "InstantiationService has been disposed".

**Cause:**
- With `cacheComponents`, Next.js 16 keeps the previous page alive in a hidden React Activity instead of unmounting it. My check confirmed this: the workspace's markup is still in the page while `/challenges` is showing.
- Hiding the page runs the editor component's cleanup, which disposes the Monaco editor. Showing it again keeps the component's old internal state, so no new editor is created.
- The editor code (`MonacoEditor.tsx` and `@monaco-editor/react`) is unchanged and predates 5A. At the committed HEAD the workspace had no link to leave it in-app, so this path couldn't occur.

**Likely fix:** a small change in `MonacoEditor.tsx` so a fresh editor is created whenever the page becomes visible again, for example a key that changes when its effects re-run. I haven't made it, because it's a workspace change outside this visual task. I recommend fixing it before committing 5A; it needs your approval.

## Remaining visual points

- **Gap under the incident report on desktop:** the metadata column is taller than the title and incident report, which leaves empty space beneath the report. It's a small gap. I can tighten it, for example by putting the metadata in one row above the button, if it bothers you.
- **Header and content edges don't line up on wide screens:** the header spans up to 1,600px, while the content column is about 1,024px, so their left edges differ at 1440px. That's normal for a reading-width layout, but say if you'd rather the content run full width.
- **Name mismatch:** the browser tab still says "BugLab · Challenge Library", which matches the "CHALLENGE LIBRARY" label.

## Task A: empty credentials in an origin

**What was wrong:** the URL parser silently drops empty credentials when it builds `href`, so these values looked like plain origins and passed `normalizeOrigin`'s exact-origin check:

| Input | `href` after parsing | Passed before |
|---|---|---|
| `https://@host` | `https://host/` | yes |
| `https://:@host` | `https://host/` | yes |
| `http://@localhost:3000` | `http://localhost:3000/` | yes |
| `user@`, `:pw@`, `a@b@` (non-empty credentials) | keeps the credentials | no, already rejected |

**Reproduced first:** I added the regression tests before changing any code, and 5 of them failed: in `normalizeOrigin`, `parseAppOrigin`, `isSameOriginRequest` in both modes, and the handler's 403 check.

**The fix** is in `src/server/diagnosis/origin.ts`, inside `normalizeOrigin`: any value containing `@` now returns `null`, with a comment explaining why. An `@` after the scheme can only be credential syntax, because paths, queries and fragments are already rejected. No exported function signature changed.

**What it affects:**
- `BUGLAB_APP_ORIGIN=https://@…` now fails closed, through `parseAppOrigin`.
- Origin headers carrying credentials are refused in both modes.
- In development mode, a `Host` header containing `@` no longer produces a usable comparison origin.
- Unchanged:
  - normal HTTPS origins;
  - uppercase hostnames and an explicit `:443`;
  - `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]` with ports;
  - the rule that requests with no `Origin` header are accepted.

**Live check** (production build):

| `BUGLAB_APP_ORIGIN` | Result |
|---|---|
| unset | the real origin and no-`Origin` requests reach validation (400); `@`, `:@` and `user:pass@` forms get 403 |
| `https://buglab.example` | only that origin is accepted; its `@` form gets 403 |
| `https://@buglab.example` | every diagnosis request gets 500 (fails closed), while `/` still returns 200 |

## Task B: the `50%20off.md` filename

**No defect.** `getModelUri` already encodes each path segment. I added regression tests to `tests/workspace/monaco-models.test.ts` that use **Monaco's real `URI` class**, not just the existing stand-in:
- `50%20off.md` becomes `…/50%2520off.md`, and Monaco decodes it back to exactly `50%20off.md`;
- it and `50 off.md` get different model keys;
- the correct model is picked whichever file opens first, and reopening returns the same model;
- 17 tricky paths round-trip with no collisions: percent escapes, `%2e%2e`, `%2f`, `%41` against `A.md`, NFC/NFD, CJK, emoji, quotes, `#?`, deep nesting.

**The tests catch a regression:** I temporarily removed the encoding, and all 4 new tests failed, along with the existing encoding test. The file was restored with no diff.

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/server/diagnosis/origin.ts` | +4 lines: the check and its comment |
| `tests/diagnosis/origin.test.ts` | 2 new tests, plus more cases in 3 existing ones |
| `tests/diagnosis/handler-origin.test.ts` | 2 more rejected origins in the 403 check |
| `tests/workspace/monaco-models.test.ts` | 4 new tests |

In total, 126 lines added and 2 removed. No session, learner-session, Challenge Library or integration files changed.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis tests | 342/342 |
| Monaco model tests | 26/26 |
| Full suite | 701/701, 0 failed, 0 skipped |

## Compatibility notes

- **The fix is stricter, never looser.** A configuration or client that relied on `https://@host` working would now be refused. Browsers never send that form, so the change mainly matters for a typo in `BUGLAB_APP_ORIGIN`, which now fails at the first diagnosis request rather than being silently accepted.
- **Habin's session handlers have their own origin check** (`isSameOrigin` in `handlers.ts`). His checks `claimed.origin`, and `new URL("https://@x").origin` drops the credentials, so his version would also accept this form. He should adopt this helper as well, which matches my earlier recommendation to use one shared origin policy.
- **The Monaco change is tests only.** Habin's extra checks on decoded paths in the loader stay compatible; they just refuse more names.

timestamp: 2026-11-04T07:52:16.949Z

The editor revisit bug is fixed. Before the fix, the editor was missing on every revisit from the second one on. After it, 6 navigation cycles on desktop and 6 on mobile all work, each with one live editor and no errors. The full suite (542/542), typecheck, lint and the build pass. The nine Milestone 5A changes are preserved, and nothing is committed.

## Root cause

It was the editor's disposal combined with the page's visibility. Model lifetime wasn't involved.

1. With `cacheComponents`, Next.js 16 keeps a visited page alive in a hidden React Activity when you navigate away. Hiding runs every effect's cleanup but keeps component state.
2. In `@monaco-editor/react` 4.7.0, the mount effect's cleanup **disposes the editor**. Its creation is guarded by state (`isEditorReady`) and a ref (`preventCreation`), both of which survive the hide.
3. When the page is shown again, the effects re-run, but `createEditor` sees `isEditorReady === true` and never makes a new editor. Its update effects then call into the disposed one, which throws "InstantiationService has been disposed", and the panel stays empty.

**Reproduced before the fix:** cycle 1 worked; cycles 2–5 had **zero editors** and threw that error.

## The fix

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/components/workspace/useRemountKey.ts` (new) | A 3-line hook returning a key that changes when the component's effects are torn down |
| `src/components/workspace/MonacoEditor.tsx` | +6 lines: `const editorKey = useRemountKey()` (with a comment) and `<Editor key={editorKey} …>` |

**How it works:**
- On hide, the cleanup bumps the key. React renders that update while the page is still hidden, so the stale editor component is replaced *before* its effects can run again.
- On show, the fresh component creates a new editor. Our existing `beforeMount` rebuilds the model from `sourceRef`, so the same model URI and the current file come back.
- On a real unmount, React ignores the update.

**What it doesn't do:** no global Monaco reset, no full-page navigation, and no extra editors. The editor is recreated only after an actual hide; normal re-renders keep the same key.

## Regression coverage

- **New test** `tests/ui/use-remount-key.test.ts`: 5 tests that run the hook's real source.
  - The key stays the same while the page is shown.
  - The key changes on hide, before the page is shown again.
  - Five hide/show cycles give keys 0–5.
  - A real unmount makes one update, which React ignores.
  - A source check that `MonacoEditor` passes the key to `<Editor>`.
- **Test helper:** `tests/helpers/react-shim.ts` gained `hide()` and `show()`, which model a hidden Activity: cleanups run but state survives, and effects re-run on show. The existing diagnosis-submission tests that use the shim still pass.
- **The tests catch the bug:** I temporarily removed the key change, and 3 of the new tests failed. The hook is restored.

## Browser results

Production build, headless Chrome. Each cycle goes library → card → workspace → header "Challenges" → library.

| Viewport | Cycles | Editor appears | Live editors | Scenario models | Opening another file | Errors | Extra full page loads |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1440 | 6 | 6/6 | 1 each time | 1 each time (no leak) | switched 6/6 | none | none |
| 375 | 6 | 6/6 | 1 each time | 1 each time | switched 6/6 | none | none |

- **State survives:** each revisit shows the file that was open when you left, such as `src/server.ts`, and opening another file switches the model every time.
- **Full library flow re-checked:**
  - 320 to 1440px: no sideways scroll and no clipped header nav;
  - keyboard order and focus outlines are unchanged;
  - clicking "Open investigation" on a second visit now loads the editor, which is what failed in the last review;
  - diagnosis returns the same 400 as before, and the workspace at `/` loads.
  - No third-party requests.

## Remaining risks

- **Scroll and cursor position reset after a revisit.** The editor is recreated, so the cursor and scroll position go back to the top. The library's own view-state cache only applies with `keepCurrentModel`, which we don't use. The open file and its content are kept.
- **Development mode creates the editor twice.** React's StrictMode runs effect cleanups once on mount in development, so the editor is created twice there. Production is unaffected.
- **Tied to `@monaco-editor/react` 4.7.0.** If a future version handles being hidden itself, the key becomes harmless but unnecessary. The hook's comment says why it exists.

## Worktree

The worktree still has the nine 5A changes, plus this fix:
- modified: `src/components/workspace/MonacoEditor.tsx` and `tests/helpers/react-shim.ts`;
- new: `src/components/workspace/useRemountKey.ts` and `tests/ui/use-remount-key.test.ts`.

Server, engine, data, lib, app, types and proxy files are unchanged. HEAD is still `eeb6ea0`, and I stopped my own server on port 3164.

## Validation on the combined code

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Full suite | **2,124/2,125**, 0 failed. The 1 skipped test scans built output; rerun after the build, it **passes** (15/15) |
| Focused: session, origin, diagnosis, loader | 1,820/1,821 (the same skip) |

| Live production smoke | `/`, `/welcome`, `/challenges` and `/challenges/challenge-001` return 200; wrong-case and unknown IDs 404; Monaco assets served |
| Live diagnosis endpoint | unchanged: same-origin 400, cross-site 403, `@`-origin 403, no-`Origin` 400 |
| Monaco revisit cycles | 5/5 ready, one live editor, no errors |

I also drove the unmounted handlers directly, using the real code through `createAppServices`.

**Origin policy on `POST /api/learner`,** with `BUGLAB_APP_ORIGIN=https://buglab.example` and the server behind a proxy at `127.0.0.1`:

| Request | Result |
|---|---|
| valid `Origin` (with or without `Sec-Fetch-Site`) | 201 |
| no `Origin` + `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` | 201 |
| no `Origin` and no `Sec-Fetch-Site`, or an empty `Origin` | 403 |
| `Origin` is cross-site, `@`, `:@`, `u:p@`, `null`, garbage or the http scheme, even with `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` | 403 |
| valid `Origin` + `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` | 403 |
| spoofed `Host` or `X-Forwarded-*` headers | 403 |
| `text/plain` body | 415 |
| prefetch | 403 |

**Cookie** (`buglab_learner`): `Path=/api; Max-Age=2592000; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Secure`. `Secure` follows the configured origin's scheme, not any request header.

**Without `BUGLAB_APP_ORIGIN`:**
- A `localhost` page talking to a `localhost` server is accepted.
- A `127.0.0.1` page is refused (it fails closed).
- An evil origin is refused even with a matching spoofed `Host`.
- Over plain http, the cookie has no `Secure`.

**Identity:**
- Resuming with a valid cookie keeps the same token.
- A forged or unknown token is never adopted; a new learner is created instead.
- Learner B sees only its own (empty) session, never A's.

**Lifecycle:**
- Submitting with no learner gives 401; before the session is started, 404; for an unknown challenge, 404; with a malformed `Idempotency-Key`, 400.
- A wrong answer gives 200 `incorrect`, with the attempt window shown (`used 1/3`).
- The same key and payload replay the stored result identically. The same key with a different payload gives 409.
- Learner B can't use A's key.
- A correct answer completes the session. The session view then includes `completion`, and the attempt history returns 2 entries with only `seq, submittedAt, rootCauseId, result, evidenceCount`.

**Leaks:**
- No `correctRootCauseId`, `keyObservations` or key-observation IDs in any response.
- No learner token or 64-hex hash in any response body.
- The resolution summary appears only in the learner's own completed session view.

## Security findings

**Critical / High:** none.

| Severity | Finding | When it matters |
|---|---|---|
| **Medium M1** | The default `MemoryStore` grows without limit: nothing calls `purgeExpired()`. Learner creation (`POST /api/learner`) is unauthenticated and not rate-limited, so once mounted, a flood of requests could exhaust memory. | Before mounting. Needs a durable store with expiry purging, and a creation rate limit. |
| **Medium M2** | The store and IP limiter live in one process (`globalThis`), so a multi-instance or serverless deployment gives "no learner" on any other instance. | Before mounting. Needs a durable adapter that passes the three contract suites (Habin's doc says the same). |
| **Low L1** | `readLearnerCookie` takes the first `buglab_learner` cookie, so if a sibling subdomain can set cookies, it could pin a browser to the attacker's learner (a login-CSRF-style risk). `SameSite=Strict` and `Path=/api` limit this. | Only matters if untrusted sibling subdomains exist. Consider stricter cookie scoping at deployment. |
| **Low L2** | Without `BUGLAB_APP_ORIGIN`, `Secure` and the expected origin come from the request URL, which can be influenced by the client-supplied `X-Forwarded-Proto` header. This fails closed and is documented. | Production must set `BUGLAB_APP_ORIGIN`; it's already on our deployment list. |
| **Low L3** | The guard functions and handler factories default to "no configured origin" (`appOrigin = null`). A future route that forgets to pass it would use the request-URL fallback. That fails closed (403s), so it's not insecure. | Route-mounting review: always build routes from `getAppServices()`. |
| **Info** | The new diagnosis handler is stricter than the live one: it refuses requests with neither `Origin` nor `Sec-Fetch-Site`. This is intended and agreed; the live endpoint is unchanged. | Decide when switching the route. |
| **Info** | The comment at `src/server/challenges/paths.ts:32–44` still describes the old unencoded editor URIs. The doc's section 8.3 has the correct "editor-side update". | Documentation follow-up for Habin. |

Read-only `GET` handlers have no origin check by design: the cookie is `SameSite=Strict` and no CORS access is granted, so another site can't read them. CSRF on writes is covered by the JSON content type, the origin policy and the prefetch refusal.

## Backend API contract (implemented, none mounted)

Every response is `no-store`, `Vary: Cookie` and `nosniff`. Errors have the shape `{ status: "error", code, message }`.

| Route | Method | Auth / guards | Success | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/api/learner` | POST | JSON body ≤1 KiB (empty or an object), origin policy, no prefetch | 201 `{learner:{state:"active",created:true}}`, or 200 when resumed, plus Set-Cookie | 400, 403, 415, 500 |
| `/api/learner` | GET | none (read-only) | 200 `{learner:{state:"none"\|"expired"\|"active"}}`; the cookie is refreshed when active | 500 |
| `/api/challenges/:id/session` | GET | learner cookie | 200 `{session:{state:"none"}}`, or `{session:{state:"active", challengeId, contentVersion, status:"active"\|"completed", startedAt, completedAt?, restartRequired, attempts:{total, wrong, window:{used, limit, remaining, resetsAt?}}, completion?}}` | 401 learner missing or expired, 404 unknown challenge |
| `/api/challenges/:id/session` | POST | small-write guards plus learner cookie | 201 when created, or 200, `{session:{state:"active", created, restarted, …}}` | 401, 404, 403, 415, 400 |
| `/api/challenges/:id/attempts` | GET | learner cookie | 200 `{attempts:[{seq, submittedAt, rootCauseId, result, evidenceCount}]}` | 401, 404 |
| `/api/challenges/:id/diagnosis` (new handler `getAppServices().diagnosis`; **the live route still uses the old handler**) | POST | JSON, strict origin, no prefetch, ≤16 KiB, learner cookie, started session; optional `Idempotency-Key` (a UUID) | 200 `correct`/`incorrect` (replays too), 400 `invalid`, 429 `rate-limited` with `Retry-After`; same body shapes as today | 401, 404 (unknown challenge or session not started), 409 `session-outdated`/`submission-id-conflict`, 413, 415, 403, 500 |

**Versioning:** an unfinished session at an older challenge version reports `restartRequired`. A `POST` to the session restarts it (`restarted: true`), and a submission against it gets 409 `session-outdated`. A completed session keeps its result and version permanently. All three issues are fixed, with regression tests. The full suite, typecheck, lint, the production build and the browser checks at 1440px and 375px all pass. One thing needs Habin's sign-off: making `serverLogId` optional required a one-line, type-only change in each of three of his test files (details below).

Everything is on the new branch `fix/frontend-compatibility-hardening`, in the worktree `C:\Users\Laptop Zone by JK\buglab-frontend-hardening`, created from `main` at `9d8fc39`. Nothing is committed.

## Root causes

**A — `serverLogId`.** The shared type said every request has a log ID, but Habin's loader accepts requests without one, and several requests may share one log line. The UI trusted the type:
- `InvestigationConsole` built a `Map` keyed by the ID, so requests without a log would collide under the key `undefined`;
- `RequestDetails` always rendered `View in Logs (…)`, even when the ID was missing or pointed at no existing log.

**B — selectors.** Five places built CSS selectors from data, `[data-…="${value}"]`. I confirmed what goes wrong in a real Chrome DOM:

| Value | Old selector | Exact match (the fix) |
|---|---|---|
| `quo"te.md` | **throws `SyntaxError`**, which broke keyboard navigation | found |
| `back\slash.md` | **not found**, because the backslash is read as an escape | found |
| brackets, Unicode, `%20` | found | found |

**C — tab IDs.** `getTabId` replaced every non-alphanumeric character with `-`, so different paths could share an ID:
- `a-b.ts`, `a_b.ts` and `a.b.ts` all became `editor-tab-a-b-ts`;
- most non-Latin names collided too.

The result was duplicate DOM IDs, so focus, scrolling and the editor panel's `aria-labelledby` could point at the wrong tab.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/types/investigation.ts` | `serverLogId?: string`, with a note that the link is optional and may be shared |
| `src/lib/log-links.ts` (new) | `linkedLogId(request, logIds)` returns the ID only if that log exists; `requestIdsByLogId` skips requests without a log, and the first request wins when several share one |
| `InvestigationConsole.tsx` | uses `requestIdsByLogId`, passes the set of existing log IDs down, and its focus lookup uses `findByData` |
| `NetworkView.tsx`, `RequestDetails.tsx` | new `logId` prop: "View in Logs (…)" appears only when the linked log exists; otherwise "None" |
| `src/lib/dom.ts` (new) | `findByData(root, attribute, value)` asks the DOM for every `[data-…]` element and compares each value exactly; the attribute **name** is validated |
| `FileExplorer.tsx`, `useListboxNavigation.ts` (2 places), `useRemovalFocus.ts` | interpolated selectors replaced with `findByData` |
| `EditorTabs.tsx` | `getTabId` keeps letters and digits and turns every other character, `-` included, into `-<hex>-`, so no two paths can share an ID; IDs use only `[A-Za-z0-9-]` |
| `tests/challenges/limits.test.ts:47`, `registry.test.ts:65`, `timestamps.test.ts:204` | **Habin's tests, type-only:** `?.length ?? 0`, an explicit `!== undefined &&` (same strength of assertion) and a `!`. Runtime behaviour is unchanged; they're needed because of the new optional type. **Please get Habin's OK**, or he can make these lines himself. |

**Totals:** 11 files modified (46 lines added, 20 removed) and 5 new files: 2 helpers and 3 test files.

**Unchanged:** server and backend code (`src/server`), challenge data, routes (`src/app`), engine, proxy, config and dependencies. No session routes were mounted, and no diagnosis security code changed.

## Regression tests

Each test was written first and **failed before the fix**: the 3 tab-ID collision tests failed outright, and the other two test files failed because their modules didn't exist yet.

| File | Tests | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/ui/dom-lookup.test.ts` | 5 | exact matching for `"`, `\`, `][`, a selector-injection string, CJK, emoji, `%20`, spaces and `#?`; no near misses; the DOM is only asked for `[data-…]`; no root or no match returns null; bad attribute names are rejected; a guard that no `querySelector` in `src/` builds a data-attribute selector from a value |
| `tests/workspace/editor-tab-ids.test.ts` | 4 | `a-b.ts`, `a_b.ts` and `a.b.ts` are distinct; 20 tricky paths are all distinct; 5,000 random paths have no collision; IDs are deterministic, keep their prefix and use a safe character set |
| `tests/workspace/log-links.test.ts` | 7 | linked, missing, empty and dangling log IDs; no `undefined` map key; first request wins for a shared log; Challenge 001 unchanged; `RequestDetails` shows the link only when the log exists, and "None" with no `undefined` text otherwise |

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| New focused tests | 16/16 |
| Full suite | **2,140/2,141**, 0 failed; the 1 skip (the build-output scan) passes once a build exists |
| Typecheck / lint | both pass (0 warnings after I tidied my own test) |
| Production build | passes |
| Answer-key leak scan | 0 hits for 39 private strings across 51 built client and prerendered files |
| Routes and diagnosis | unchanged: `/`, `/welcome`, `/challenges` and `/challenges/challenge-001` return 200; wrong-case and unknown IDs 404; diagnosis 400 / 403 / 403 as before |

**Browser** (production build, both 1440px and 375px, no console errors):
- **Explorer:** ArrowDown moves focus from `logs` to `logs/app.log`.
- **Editor tabs:** IDs such as `editor-tab-src-2f-routes-2f-auth-2e-ts` are unique; arrow keys move focus between tabs; the editor panel's `aria-labelledby` points at the active tab.
- **Network → "View in Logs (log-03)":** opens the Logs tab with `log-03` focused.
- **Log list:** ArrowDown moves to `log-04`.
- **Log → "View in Network":** focuses `req-01`.
- **Evidence:** removing `log:log-01` with the keyboard removes it and moves focus to `network:req-01`'s Remove button.

  My first run of this check used a key event that doesn't activate buttons, so it reported a false failure; with the corrected event it passes.
- **Library → Workspace → Library:** 4/4 cycles at each width; the editor loads and file switching works.

## Remaining risks

1. **Habin's three test lines** need his agreement, as above.
2. **The "no request without a log" case is covered only by unit tests.** Challenge 001's data was off-limits, and every one of its requests has a log, so the browser couldn't show it.
3. **Tab IDs for non-Latin names are longer now**, for example `-65e5--672c-…`. They're opaque DOM IDs that nobody sees, and still valid.
4. **`findByData` scans every element with that attribute.** The lists are small (one challenge's files, logs and requests), so it's negligible.

I stopped my own server on port 3170. No other worktree, branch or remote was touched.

## Tab IDs can never collide

I proved this rather than relying on random testing, and it holds, so no code change was needed:
- **Strings to code points:** the string iterator turns distinct strings into distinct code-point sequences. A valid surrogate pair becomes one code point; a lone surrogate keeps its own value.
- **Code points to the ID:** letters and digits are kept, and everything else, `-` included, becomes `-<hex>-`. A bare `-` only ever marks a code, so the ID decodes back unambiguously.

The new tests make this executable:
- **Decoder round-trip:** a decoder in the test turns every ID back into exactly its path. Covered cases include:
  - `""`, `-`, `-2d-`, U+0000;
  - `é` against `e` + combining accent (NFC against NFD), `Å` against the Ångström sign;
  - emoji, ZWJ sequences and flags;
  - lone and reversed surrogates;
  - zero-width characters and BOM, tab and newline;
  - quotes, backslashes and brackets, `%20` and `%41`, the `ﬁ` ligature, CJK, and a 300-character name.
- **Every single UTF-16 code unit,** all 65,536 including lone surrogates, gets its own ID that decodes back.
- **Every string of up to 4 characters** over an alphabet heavy in dashes and hex digits (11,111 strings) has no collision and round-trips.
- **The tests catch regressions:** encoding UTF-16 code units instead of code points fails 3 tests, and leaving `-` unescaped fails 3. The code was restored after each check.

BugLab — Frontend Learner-Session Integration, Phase 1

BASE:
origin/main at f9bbf46f5bfd4a8a2efbb6f2f42c616fb50eccca

OBJECTIVE:
Implement the frontend foundation for persistent learner sessions, without mounting or activating backend routes.

Create an isolated worktree and branch:
feature/frontend-learner-session-client

SCOPE:

1. Inspect the existing backend contracts in:
   - src/server/session/*
   - src/server/challenges/*
   - src/server/app-services.ts

2. Implement a typed frontend API client for:
   - GET/POST /api/learner
   - GET/POST /api/challenges/:id/session
   - GET /api/challenges/:id/attempts
   - POST /api/challenges/:id/diagnosis

3. Handle HTTP errors explicitly:
   - 400 malformed request
   - 401 missing or expired learner
   - 403 Origin/CSRF rejection
   - 404 unknown challenge or missing session
   - 409 outdated session or idempotency conflict
   - 413 payload too large
   - 415 unsupported content type
   - 429 rate limiting, including Retry-After
   - 500 server failure

4. Implement retry-safe diagnosis idempotency:
   - Generate one UUID per logical submission.
   - Reuse that UUID only when retrying the identical submission.
   - Generate a new UUID when the submission changes.
   - Never persist or expose learner cookie tokens.

5. Design a session initialization coordinator:
   - Read existing learner/session state.
   - Create a learner and start a session when necessary.
   - Detect restartRequired and version changes.
   - Avoid duplicate initialization calls.
   - Keep completion restoration separate for Phase 2.

6. Add comprehensive unit and integration tests using mocked HTTP responses and the real backend response contracts.

7. Preserve the current working Challenge 001 experience.

- Do not mount any backend routes.
- Do not switch the live diagnosis handler.

Report the architecture, exact changed files, tests, validation and any backend-contract questions.

The learner-session client foundation is built and fully tested, including against Habin's real backend handlers. Nothing is activated: no route is mounted, and no page or component uses the client.

It's on the new branch `feature/frontend-learner-session-client`, in the worktree `C:\Users\Laptop Zone by JK\buglab-learner-client`, created from `main` at `f9bbf46`. Nothing is committed.

## Architecture

There are four small modules in `src/lib/learner-session/`, plus a public type file. They're browser-safe: no imports from `src/server`, no cookie or storage access.

| Module | Role |
|---|---|
| `src/types/learner-session.ts` | The API as the browser sees it: `ChallengeSession`, `SessionCompletion`, `AttemptSummary`, `LearnerState`, `ApiError` / `ApiErrorKind`, `ApiResult<T>`. These mirror the server's views, and the contract test keeps them in step. |
| `parse.ts` | Field-by-field shape checks for every response; a malformed 2xx body becomes `invalid-response`, never data. Session views go through an allow-list, so unknown or internal fields are dropped. |
| `api.ts` | `createLearnerSessionApi({ fetch?, timeoutMs? })`: the methods `getLearner`, `startLearner`, `getSession`, `startSession`, `listAttempts` and `submitDiagnosis` (more below). |
| `idempotency.ts` | `createSubmissionKeys()`: `keyFor(submission)` returns the same UUID for the same submission and a new one for any change; `reset()` forgets it. Keys live only in memory. |
| `coordinator.ts` | `createSessionCoordinator(api, challengeId)`: `ensure()` and `invalidate()` (more below). |

**`api.ts` in more detail:**
- **Requests:** same-origin credentials and a timeout. POSTs send JSON (`{}` for learner and session). The challenge ID is encoded as a single path segment.
- **Results:** every method returns an `ApiResult` instead of throwing. Only the caller's own abort rethrows, as the existing diagnosis client does.
- **`submitDiagnosis` results:** the four answers the workspace shows come back as `{ kind: "response" }`: 200 `correct`/`incorrect`, 400 `invalid` and 429 `rate-limited`. Anything else is `{ kind: "error" }`.
- **Error mapping:**

  | Status | Kind | Server codes |
  |---|---|---|
  | 400 | `bad-request` | |
  | 401 | `unauthorized` | `learner-missing`, `learner-expired` |
  | 403 | `forbidden` | |
  | 404 | `not-found` | `unknown-challenge`, `session-missing` |
  | 409 | `conflict` | `session-outdated`, `submission-id-conflict` |
  | 413 | `payload-too-large` | |
  | 415 | `unsupported-media-type` | |
  | 429 | `rate-limited` | `retryAfterSeconds` from `Retry-After` (seconds or an HTTP date), falling back to the body |
  | 5xx | `server` | |

  Other cases: no response gives `network`, a timeout gives `timeout`, and an unrecognised status or body gives `invalid-response`.

**The idempotency fingerprint** matches the server's own notion of the same submission: the root cause, the explanation normalised with the shared `normalizeExplanation`, and the de-duplicated, sorted evidence. So reordered evidence or CRLF line endings keep the key (the server would treat them as the same), while any real change gets a new key.

**The coordinator:**
1. It reads the session. If the session is active and current, it's ready.
2. On a 401, it creates a learner, then starts the session.
3. If there's no session, or `restartRequired` is set, it starts the session, and the server restarts an outdated one.
4. If the learner expires between the read and the start, it recreates the learner **once**, never looping.

Concurrent `ensure()` calls share one run, and a ready result is kept. A failure isn't kept, so the next call retries. The ready result reports `learnerCreated`, `sessionCreated`, `restarted` and `versionChanged`. A completed session's `completion` is passed through untouched; restoring it is Phase 2.

## Changed files

- **Modified:** `src/lib/diagnosis/response.ts`. `isFeedback` and `isAttemptStatus` are now exported for reuse, with no behaviour change.
- **New source:** the four modules above and `src/types/learner-session.ts`.
- **New tests:** `tests/learner-session/api.test.ts`, `coordinator.test.ts`, `idempotency.test.ts` and `contract.test.ts`.
- **Unchanged:** `src/server`, `src/app`, `src/components`, `src/engine`, `src/data` and the proxy.

## Tests (61 new)

- **`api.test.ts` (32):**
  - request shapes;
  - every status with its codes, `Retry-After` in seconds, HTTP-date and body forms;
  - malformed 2xx bodies;
  - non-JSON error bodies;
  - network failure, timeout and caller abort;
  - diagnosis answers, including an answer whose HTTP status contradicts its body.
- **`coordinator.test.ts` (13):** every initialization path; no loop on a repeated 401; non-retried failures; concurrent calls de-duplicated; ready results kept; failures retried; `invalidate()` reporting the version change; completed sessions passed through.
- **`idempotency.test.ts` (9):** retries reuse the key; every change gets a new key; returning to an earlier answer gets a new key; the server's sameness rules; `reset()`; the UUID v4 format, including the `getRandomValues` fallback.
- **`contract.test.ts` (10), against the real `createAppServices` handlers:**
  - a fresh browser makes 3 calls, then 0; a returning browser makes 1;
  - a content change is detected and the session restarted;
  - unknown challenge;
  - wrong answer, retry replays (nothing recorded), reused key gives a 409 conflict, correct answer;
  - the completed session view and attempt history parse correctly;
  - the 3-attempt window gives a 429 rate-limited answer with `retryAfterSeconds`;
  - real 401, 404 and 413 responses, a malformed key gives 400 `invalid`, and a missing `Origin` gives 403;
  - **leaks:** no learner token and no private evaluation data in anything the client returns;
  - **guards:** the client code never touches cookies or storage and imports nothing from the server, and no page, component or engine file imports it yet.
- **Mutation checks:** "a new key on every call" fails 3 tests, and "no de-duplication" fails 3. Both files were restored.

One existing guard of Habin's (`tests/session/source-guards.test.ts`) at first flagged my type file, because its header **comment** mentioned the server session folder's path. I reworded the comment; his test is untouched.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| New focused tests | 61/61 |
| Full suite | **2,206/2,206**, 0 failed, 0 skipped |
| Typecheck / lint | both pass |
| Production build | passes; the build-output scan passes (15/15) |
| Route list | unchanged: the only API route is `/api/challenges/[challengeId]/diagnosis` |
| Live server check | `/api/learner`, `/session` and `/attempts` return **404**; pages, the diagnosis endpoint and Monaco behave as before (3/3 navigation cycles) |
| Leak scan | 0 hits in 51 built client and prerendered files (answer-key strings, field names, `buglab_learner`); no client bundle references `/api/learner` |

## Backend contract questions for Habin

1. **A malformed `Idempotency-Key`** returns 400 `invalid` with `field: "body"`, so it looks like a validation error on the learner's answer. That's really a client bug. Would a distinct `code` be better? The client handles either way.
2. **Submitting after completion** returns 200 with the stored `correct` result, not a 409. Is that the intended long-term behaviour? It affects the Phase 2 user experience.
3. **The in-memory store loses everything on restart.** A submission then gets a 401 or a 404 `session-missing`. Phase 2 will respond by calling `coordinator.invalidate()` and re-initializing. Is that the behaviour you expect?
4. **The IP-limit 429** carries no `attempts`, while the attempt-window 429 does. Is that intended? It's fine for the client.
5. **Retrying a completed challenge** is still undecided: `restartRequired` is always false once completed.

## Left for Phase 2

- Mount the routes, once Habin's M1 and M2 are done.
- Wire the coordinator and key tracker into the workspace, and switch the diagnosis client to this API.
- On 401, `session-missing` or `session-outdated`: invalidate and re-initialize. On `restarted`, clear local evidence, notes and hypotheses.
- Restore a completed session from `completion`.
- Show the attempt window, and optionally the history.

I stopped my own server on port 3171 and touched no other worktree or branch.

# BUGLAB — SPRINT 6: DYNAMIC CHALLENGE DISCOVERY + AUTHENTICATION + ADMIN FOUNDATION

You are acting as the lead full-stack engineer and product designer for BugLab, a production-oriented debugging investigation platform.

We want to move quickly and deliver a substantial, cohesive implementation in ONE development sprint, not a series of tiny tasks.

## BASELINE

Repository: syedamahnoor-sm/buglab

Expected origin/main:
f94a39f98b2c051b30cb87082dae8ed25cac8d14

Create a NEW isolated worktree and branch:

feature/challenge-discovery-identity-foundation

Do not modify existing worktrees or Habin's branches.

First inspect the repository architecture, challenge registry, catalog data, existing learner-session backend/client, routes, tests and security conventions.

Do not assume any API, schema, package or capability already exists without inspecting it.

## PRIMARY OBJECTIVE

Transform the Challenge Library into a compelling, scalable discovery experience while establishing a secure foundation for learner accounts, role-based access control and future admin publishing.

Implement as much of the following scope as can be completed safely and thoroughly in this sprint.

Do not stop after writing a plan. Implement, test and report working code.

---

# PART A — DYNAMIC CHALLENGE CATALOG

Create a single source of truth for public challenge discovery.

Requirements:

1. Reuse the existing challenge registry and catalog infrastructure wherever possible.
2. Eliminate hardcoded challenge-card definitions.
3. Automatically discover all published, playable challenges.
4. Adding a new challenge through the supported registration mechanism must not require changing the Challenge Library UI.
5. Support public metadata:
   - ID and slug
   - Title
   - Short description
   - Category
   - Difficulty
   - Technologies/tags
   - Estimated completion time
   - Publication status
   - Featured status, if supported
6. Define a clear metadata validation contract.
7. Ensure incomplete, draft and archived challenges cannot be launched as published challenges.
8. Never expose answer keys, hidden evaluation rules, private server logs or internal diagnosis data through the public catalog.

Preserve Challenge 001 exactly as a playable investigation.

Add tests proving that a newly registered published challenge automatically appears in the catalog and that an unpublished challenge does not.

Do not invent playable scenarios merely to fill the page.

---

# PART B — CHALLENGE LIBRARY V2

Build a polished, responsive discovery experience consistent with BugLab's existing dark investigation-themed design.

Implement:

1. Category sidebar with icons and dynamic challenge counts.
2. All Challenges category.
3. Search by title, description, technology and tags.
4. Difficulty filtering.
5. Category filtering.
6. Technology/tag filtering.
7. Sort options, including recommended, newest and difficulty.
8. Featured Investigation section.
9. Continue Investigating section with a safe empty state until progress is integrated.
10. Recommended for You section, initially using transparent, deterministic catalog-based recommendations.
11. Beginner-friendly section.
12. Related challenges on challenge details where supported.

**Verdict: GO for committing Sprint 6.** I found one real gap, which was that the diagnosis endpoint ignored publication status. It's now closed and tested. Nothing has been committed, pushed or merged.

## What updates automatically when a second challenge is registered
Adding a `{ scenario, listing }` entry to `REGISTERED_CHALLENGES` updates all of these with no other changes:
- the catalog;
- the library cards;
- category counts;
- search and filters;
- the featured and recommended sections;
- `generateStaticParams`;
- the proxy allow-list.

**Still manual for each new challenge:**
1. An answer key in `createDefaultRegistry()` (`src/server/diagnosis/registry.ts`).
2. A challenge entry in Habin's `default-registry.ts`.

Both steps are now enforced. CI fails if a published challenge has no answer key, if its answer-key data doesn't match the scenario, or if Habin's registry differs from the catalog in IDs, public content or content versions.

## Gap fixed
- **Problem:** the live diagnosis route accepted any challenge that had an answer key, published or not. A draft or archived challenge with a key could be submitted, and a correct answer would return its resolution.
- **Fix:** `src/server/diagnosis/published.ts` adds `restrictToPublished()`. The route now uses `restrictToPublished(createDefaultRegistry())`, a 3-line change to the route file.
- **Result:** an unpublished challenge is treated as unknown and gets a 404 with no attempt cookie. The 415 and 403 checks still run first, and Challenge 001 behaves as before.
- **Tests:** `tests/catalog/integration.test.ts` has 10 tests. When I removed the gate as a check, the test written to catch it failed, as intended.

## Other confirmations
- **Unpublished challenges are unreachable** through public pages, routes, the proxy and the diagnosis API.
- **Scale:** 30 challenges across six categories render with every section, correct counts and unique IDs, with no UI changes.
- **Validation after the fix:**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Tests | 2,304/2,304 pass |
| Typecheck, lint | pass |
| Production build | pass, same routes as before |
| `git diff --check` | clean |
| Leak scan on the new build | 0 hits for answer-key text or server-only names |

- **Live production checks:**
  - `/`, `/welcome`, `/challenges` and `/challenges/challenge-001` return 200.
  - `CHALLENGE-001` and `challenge-999` return 404.
  - Diagnosis for Challenge 001 still gives 400 for same-origin requests and 403 for cross-site ones; unknown challenges get 404.

## Remaining limitations (none block the commit)
1. **Habin's registry has no publication status.** It's consistent today only because every registered challenge is published. When his routes are mounted, they'll need the same gate.
2. **Account-to-learner linking needs a server-side way to turn the learner cookie into a learner ID.** Habin's service doesn't offer this yet, so it needs coordinating with him.
3. **PostgreSQL:** the auth types fit cleanly (UUID-compatible string IDs; roles as an enum or check constraint). The link table needs UNIQUE constraints on both `accountId` and `learnerId`.
4. **Auth and admin stay inactive**, as specified. There is no auth provider, no durable store and no admin routes.
5. **There's no way to preview a draft in development.** Drafts can only be seen through tests.

When you approve the commit, per `CLAUDE.md` I'll include `.claude-logs/` with it.

# BUGLAB — SPRINT 7: 30 FULLY PLAYABLE DEBUGGING INVESTIGATIONS

Repository: syedamahnoor-sm/buglab

Expected origin/main:
ac863c60b37a3ff89889b05731babf31ab1f39bc

Create a NEW isolated worktree and branch:

feature/challenge-content-expansion

Do not modify existing worktrees or Habin's branches.

## MISSION

Expand BugLab from one playable debugging challenge to at least 30 complete, distinct, production-quality investigations across six categories.

This is a substantial implementation sprint. Work autonomously through authoring, integration, testing and browser validation. Do not stop after planning.

Preserve the existing Challenge 001 unchanged.

## TARGET DISTRIBUTION

Create five playable investigations in each category:

1. Authentication & Authorization — 5 total
2. APIs & Backend — 5 total
3. Frontend & React — 5 total
4. Databases & Data Integrity — 5 total
5. Security & Vulnerabilities — 5 total
6. Performance & Production — 5 total

Challenge 001 counts toward Authentication & Authorization.

Therefore implement 29 new investigations.

Distribute difficulty across beginner, intermediate and advanced. Avoid making every scenario equally complex.

## PHASE A — AUDIT AND AUTHORING FOUNDATION

Inspect:

- Existing Challenge 001 scenario structure
- Public catalog and validation
- Existing diagnosis registry and answer-key structure
- Habin's challenge registry and content-version contracts
- Monaco file and tab handling
- Logs, network requests and evidence systems
- Publication gate
- Challenge Library filters and recommendations
- Existing test helpers and fixtures

Build a maintainable authoring workflow that minimizes repetitive registration steps.

Requirements:

- Preserve public/private separation.
- Keep answer keys and evaluation logic server-only.
- Preserve Habin's registry contracts.
- Detect missing registrations, mismatched content versions and invalid evidence references.
- Validate all published challenges automatically.
- Do not require editing Library UI components when adding challenges.
- Document how a developer authors, registers and publishes a new challenge.

Do not introduce dynamic imports or module patterns that leak private challenge data into client bundles.

## PHASE B — CREATE 29 NEW INVESTIGATIONS

Every investigation must contain:

1. Unique challenge ID and title.
2. Category and difficulty.
3. Description and realistic incident background.
4. Technology tags and estimated duration.
5. A coherent buggy codebase with multiple relevant files.
6. Realistic application/server logs.
7. Relevant network requests and responses where appropriate.
8. Investigative clues and evidence references.
9. Multiple plausible root-cause options.
10. One defensible correct root cause.
11. Server-only answer key and evaluation rules.
12. Meaningful feedback for correct and incorrect diagnoses.
13. Consistent content version.
14. Complete catalog registration.
15. Complete private diagnosis registration.
16. Complete learner-session registry registration.
17. A playable challenge route.
18. Automated validation tests.

All challenge content must be original.

Avoid trivial variations of the same bug.

Use different debugging techniques: tracing requests, reading logs, comparing code paths, investigating authorization, analyzing SQL, identifying race conditions, debugging React state, examining caching and diagnosing production failures.

Make each investigation internally consistent. The evidence must actually support its intended diagnosis.

Do not fabricate real-world customer incidents or claim fictional logs are real production records.

## PHASE C — CONTENT QUALITY

## How a new challenge is added

1. Create `src/data/challenge-NNN/index.ts` using `defineChallenge`. It numbers the logs and requests, writes the log file, and fills in each request's time, method, path, status and default headers from its server log line.
2. Create `answer-key.server.ts` next to it using `defineAnswerKey`. It refers to evidence by position and is checked against the scenario when the server loads.
3. Add one line to each registration list: `src/data/catalog/index.ts` (public) and `src/server/content/index.ts` (server-only).
4. Add a revision pin in `tests/challenges/revision-pin.test.ts`. The test prints the exact entry to add.

The live diagnosis registry and Habin's registry both load the same server-only list. A new suite, `tests/content/authored-challenges.test.ts`, checks every challenge automatically:
- the two registration lists name the same challenges, in the same order;
- each request agrees with its server log line, and logs and requests are in time order;
- the challenge has enough code files, log lines and choices;
- no answer leaks into public content, and no two challenges share content;
- grading works through the live endpoint for every option.

# BUGLAB — SPRINT 7B: COMPLETE THE 30-CHALLENGE LIBRARY

Repository: syedamahnoor-sm/buglab

Expected origin/main:
1e330f8b06d6980b26b8e580ae2049d56fa7730c

Create a NEW isolated worktree and branch:

feature/challenge-content-completion

Do not modify existing worktrees or other branches.

## MISSION

Complete the four missing BugLab investigations and bring the published challenge count from 26 to exactly 30.

The existing 26 challenges have passed 2,486 tests, desktop/mobile browser validation, production build and answer-key leak checks.

Preserve them.

## PHASE 1 — INSPECT THE EXISTING AUTHORING SYSTEM

Read:

- docs/authoring/challenges.md
- src/lib/authoring/
- src/server/content/
- src/data/catalog/index.ts
- Existing representative challenge scenarios and answer keys
- tests/content/authored-challenges.test.ts
- Revision pin tests
- Diagnosis evaluator and publication gate
- CLAUDE.md and .claude-logs/ requirements

Understand the complete authoring contract before creating new scenarios.

Do not redesign the architecture unnecessarily.

## PHASE 2 — IMPLEMENT THE FOUR MISSING CHALLENGES

Work on one challenge at a time.

### Challenge 023 — The Configuration That Went Public

Category: Security & Vulnerabilities
Difficulty: Beginner

A development team accidentally includes server-only configuration metadata in a client-side application build.

The learner investigates environment variable naming, build configuration and public/server module boundaries.

Use fictional placeholder configuration only. Do not include real credentials, working secrets or instructions for extracting sensitive data.

The diagnosis should identify the incorrect client/server configuration boundary and recommend keeping private configuration server-side.

### Challenge 024 — The Redirect That Went Somewhere Else

Category: Security & Vulnerabilities
Difficulty: Intermediate

An authentication callback sometimes sends users to an unintended destination because its redirect validation is incomplete.

The learner examines application routing logic, configuration, sanitized request logs and unit-test results.

Focus on safe allow-list validation and correct fallback routing. Do not include phishing destinations, exploit payloads or attack instructions.

### Challenge 025 — The Missing Audit Trail

Category: Security & Vulnerabilities
Difficulty: Advanced

An administrative account-setting change succeeds, but its expected audit event is missing.

The learner traces application event handling, asynchronous jobs, database writes and monitoring evidence to identify why the audit record was not persisted.

Use fictional users, synthetic events and non-sensitive logs.

### Challenge 027 — The Growing Memory Footprint

Category: Performance & Production
Difficulty: Advanced

A long-running Node.js service gradually increases its memory consumption during normal operation.

The learner investigates lifecycle management, resource cleanup, metrics, application logs and source code.

Focus on identifying retained resources and correcting cleanup logic.

## PHASE 3 — FULL PLAYABILITY CONTRACT

Each challenge must have:

1. Original, coherent incident background.
2. Multiple relevant source files.
3. Realistic application logs.
4. Network observations where appropriate.
5. Evidence references consistent with the code and logs.
6. Plausible root-cause options.
7. One uniquely supported correct diagnosis.
8. Server-only answer key.
9. Meaningful investigation hints.
10. Correct and incorrect diagnosis feedback.
11. Matching content version and revision pin.
12. Public catalog registration.
13. Server-only content registration.
14. Compatibility with Habin's learner-session registry.
15. Automated content and grading tests.

Use the existing defineChallenge and defineAnswerKey helpers.

Do not create placeholders or publish incomplete scenarios.

TITLE:

Security & Vulnerabilities

An organization changes an employee's role from Administrator to Viewer.

The backend correctly updates the user's role and enforces Viewer permissions.

However, the employee's existing browser session continues displaying administrative controls until the page is refreshed.

The learner investigates the discrepancy between the server's current permissions and the frontend's cached permission state.

The React application retains stale permission information in a client-side cache after a role change.

The cache is not invalidated or refreshed when the effective permissions change.

IMPORTANT SECURITY BOUNDARY:

Administrative operations must remain forbidden to the Viewer.

The bug is stale frontend permission presentation, not an authorization bypass.

- Server-only answer key.
- Resolution explanation.

Advanced

The frontend waits for a large analytics API response, while the backend retrieves unnecessary records and repeatedly computes aggregates.

ROOT CAUSE:

The analytics endpoint fetches the complete dataset and performs repeated application-level calculations rather than using efficient database-side aggregation and bounded result retrieval.

- Analytics API implementation.

The library is complete: **30 published challenges, 5 in each of the six categories**, every check passes, and the recommendation is **GO for committing Sprint 7C**. Nothing is committed, pushed or merged.

## 023 · The Permission That Never Updated (Security, Intermediate)
- **Incident:** an employee is moved from Administrator to Viewer. Their open tab keeps showing Archive, Delete and Manage members for nine minutes, and every click fails.
- **What the learner must establish:** the server was right the whole time. It checks the current role on every request, so every admin action after the change got 403 and was logged as `role=viewer`.
- **The actual bug:** the React app loaded permissions once, kept them in a cache that lasts for the whole page, and never asked again. On a 403 it only showed a generic error message.
- **Evidence:** 8 files, 11 log lines, 5 requests and 4 key observations. Two of the wrong options assume the server let the user through; the other two blame an unsaved role change or an HTTP cache.

## 027 · The Dashboard That Slowed Down (Performance, Advanced)
- **Incident:** a 90-day analytics summary has slowed from 0.8 s to 4.8 s over a month, with no deploys.
- **The bug:**
  - The endpoint ignores the 90-day range and loads all 1,342,118 events.
  - It filters that whole list once per day: 90 × 1,342,118 = 120,790,620 rows scanned.
  - It returns all of them in a 40 MB response, although the dashboard shows only 20.
- **The numbers agree:**
  - The query, aggregation and serialisation times (1,410 + 2,980 + 410 ms) add up to the 4,806 ms request.
  - Latency rises in step with the rows loaded (210k, 524k, 1.33M).
- **Evidence against the other options:**
  - The index is used.
  - The database is at 22% CPU.
  - A widget that aggregates in SQL takes 31 ms.
  - Rendering takes 120 ms.
- **Size:** 7 files, 13 log lines, 2 requests and 7 key observations.

## One fix during validation
My Sprint 6 identity guard test flagged 023, because the scenario's simulated app stored its permissions in browser storage. It was a false positive, but rather than weaken the guard, I changed the scenario to keep the permissions in memory. The behaviour (a refresh fixes it) is the same. Because 023's resolution text changed, I updated its revision pin to the new digest. It stays at revision 1, since 023 has never been released.
